robot.name: Kepler K2 Bumblebee
robot.generation: K2 'Bumblebee' industrial humanoid (company refers to its fifth-generation humanoid robot program)
robot.status_notes: K2 Bumblebee is priced at a $30,000 base model or RMB 248,000 per unit and Kepler announced mass production and customer shipments on 2025-09-27. BigGo Finance reported confirmed orders above 47 million yuan by 2026-05-22, but 2025 revenue was only 4.34 million yuan and the company was acquired by Hangzhou Kelin. No public web checkout was found; purchase appears to be via contact sales.

payload.original_value: 30 kg with both arms (15 kg per arm)
payload.notes: Source 1 says 15 kg per arm and up to 30 kg with both arms.

runtime.original_value: Up to 8 hours on a single one-hour charge
runtime.notes: Company claim repeated across sources 1, 4 and 5.

battery.notes: Battery capacity was not published in any reviewed source.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Source 1 reports 52 total degrees of freedom.

walking_speed.notes: No walking speed was found. Sources describe steady autonomous mobility, fluid humanlike motion, and straight-knee bipedal gait but do not give m/s.

hands.description: Kepler Dexterous Hands with 11 degrees of freedom per hand, 25 force-sensing contact points per finger, and a six-axis force/torque sensor at the wrist.
hands.force_feedback: 6-axis wrist force/torque sensor and 25 force-sensing contact points per finger (company claim)

actuators.description: Hybrid series-parallel architecture combining planetary roller screw linear actuators and rotary actuators; company claims 81.3% energy efficiency and millimeter-level precision for fine motor tasks.

availability.notes: The Robot Report lists a $30,000 base price. Source 4 lists RMB 248,000 per unit. Purchase path is contact sales; no public web store found.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: K2 has 11-DoF hands with 25 force-sensing points per finger and a 6-axis wrist force/torque sensor. Kepler claims millimeter-level precision via rotary actuators and 15 kg per arm / 30 kg dual-arm payload. Trade-show and press-release demos show gestures, thumbs-up, waving and parade routines, but no long-horizon dexterity tasks are disclosed in the reviewed sources.
caveats: No independent dexterity benchmark or published task success rates.
Manipulation demos are company-described trade-show interactions, not detailed industrial tasks.
No transcript exists for the official on-the-job video titles.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Source 1 says K2 navigated ICRA 2025 with 'steady, autonomous mobility' according to Kepler. Source 4 and Source 5 describe a layered VLA+ model interpreting natural language commands for tasks including sorting, assembly and guided tours. No independent autonomy audit, intervention logs or teleoperation disclosure for most demos was found.
caveats: Autonomy statements are company claims, not independently verified.
Teleoperation status is not disclosed for most demos.
No success rate or failure count published.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Source 5 describes a video in which K2 navigates bricks, plastic surfaces and grass and remains stable under external pushes. Source 1 and Source 3 describe humanlike, straight-knee bipedal gait and robot-parade walking. Source 4 production video includes straight-knee gait, obstacle navigation and dynamic performance evaluations.
caveats: Gait demo is described in a paid press release, not independently captured.
No raw balance, fall-rate or disturbance metrics published.
Videos noted as no-transcript in the source list should not be used for claims beyond their titles.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Source 4 and Source 5 say K2 uses a layered VLA+ model to interpret semantic commands and carry out tasks. Source 3 describes an integrated multimodal interaction engine combining visual, auditory and tactile data, plus developer tools for vision, navigation and voice.
caveats: No public perception benchmark, object-recognition accuracy or scene-understanding result found.
Descriptions come from company press releases.

human_interaction.summary: At ICRA/IROS, K2 reportedly greeted attendees with natural gestures, responded with thumbs-up and wave, and interacted fluidly with other robotic systems. No end-user conversational or instruction-following evaluation was found.
caveats: Trade-show interactions are described by company-published or company-influenced sources.
No robust human-robot interaction study or reliability metric found.

endurance_reliability.summary: Kepler claims up to 8 hours operation on a one-hour charge, near-zero static power consumption from roller screw actuators, 81.3% energy efficiency, and production-video content showing high/low-temperature tests, aging trials, obstacle navigation and thousands of hours of continuous uptime without failure.
caveats: Endurance figures are company claims; no independent endurance log or raw mean time between failures published.
Production video claims come from a press-release description, not an independent audit.
Financial disclosures show very low 2025 revenue, raising uncertainty about long-term support.

human_environment_fit.summary: K2 is human-sized at 175 cm and 75 kg, designed for industrial factory floors with a straight-knee bipedal gait and hybrid actuator design. The company markets it for manufacturing, logistics, high-risk operations and exhibitions.
caveats: No safety certification or third-party human-proximity safety assessment found.
No detailed workspace safety or collaborative-operation standard disclosed.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Kepler announced mass production and customer shipments on 2025-09-27, with framework agreements for several thousand units. BigGo Finance reports confirmed orders above 47 million yuan and an official Kepler video title refers to an 'On-the-Job Log — Zhaofeng Motor'. The same financial reporting shows 2025 revenue was only about 4.34 million yuan with large net losses.
caveats: No deployed unit count, operating hours, output metrics or customer press release were found.
The Zhaofeng Motor reference is a video title only; no transcript or independent confirmation is available.
Framework agreements are not the same as delivered units.

accessibility_value.summary: Kepler lists a $30,000 base price and RMB 248,000 unit price, intended to lower adoption barriers for mass production. Purchase path appears to be contact sales, not an online store.
caveats: Prices are company listings, not independently confirmed.
No public warranty, service package or total cost of ownership found.
Company financial instability may affect value and support.

evidence_items.title: K2 Bumblebee physical specifications at ICRA 2025
evidence_items.claim: K2 Bumblebee is 175 cm tall, weighs 75 kg, has 52 degrees of freedom and more than 80 integrated sensors.
evidence_items.notes: The Robot Report repeats Kepler's stated specifications.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Defines size, weight and DoF for comparison.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Purpose-built for industrial settings, the K2 Bumblebee is 175 cm (68.9 in.) tall, weighs 75 kg (165.3 lb.), and features 52 degrees of freedom and more than 80 integrated sensors.
evidence_items.source_location: The Robot Report article, 'Kepler designs K2 humanoid for industrial use' section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company specification as reported by trade media; not independently measured.

evidence_items.title: K2 payload, runtime and precision claims
evidence_items.claim: K2 supports 15 kg per arm and up to 30 kg with both arms, up to 8 hours of operation on a one-hour charge, and millimeter-level precision for fine motor tasks.
evidence_items.notes: These are company performance claims, not independent measurements.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Payload and runtime are important for industrial tasks.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Combined with its innovative series-parallel architecture and advanced actuation system, Kepler said the K2 supports payloads of 15 kg (33.1 lb.) per arm and up to 30 kg (66.1 lb.) with both arms.
evidence_items.source_location: The Robot Report article, 'Kepler designs K2 humanoid for industrial use' section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Runtime and precision from the same source are not independently tested.

evidence_items.title: K2 Dexterous Hands
evidence_items.claim: K2 has proprietary Dexterous Hands with 11 degrees of freedom per hand, 25 force-sensing contact points per finger, and a six-axis force/torque sensor at the wrist.
evidence_items.notes: Detailed hand hardware claim from Kepler via The Robot Report.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Hand dexterity is a key differentiation for manipulation.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The Bumblebee also includes Kepler’s proprietary Dexterous Hands, each featuring 11 degrees of freedom, 25 force-sensing contact points per finger, and a six-axis force/torque sensor at the wrist.
evidence_items.source_location: The Robot Report article, 'Kepler designs K2 humanoid for industrial use' section
evidence_items.verification_notes: No independent hand dexterity benchmark found.

evidence_items.title: K2 price and workload claim
evidence_items.claim: The base model of K2 Bumblebee is priced at $30,000 and can perform the equivalent workload of about 1.5 full-time human workers, according to Kepler.
evidence_items.notes: Productivity equivalence is a company claim with no public evidence.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Price and productivity matter for value assessment.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The base model of the K2 Bumblebee is priced at $30,000 and can perform the equivalent workload of approximately 1.5 full-time human workers in comparable timeframes, according to Kepler.
evidence_items.source_location: The Robot Report article, 'Humanoids take steps toward production' section
evidence_items.verification_notes: No independent productivity study or customer return-on-investment data found.

evidence_items.title: ICRA 2025 trade-show mobility and interaction claim

evidence_items.source_location: The Robot Report article, ICRA 2025 section

evidence_items.title: K2 production video durability showcase

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Kepler K2 Bumblebee is a 175 cm, 75 kg industrial humanoid with hybrid actuators, 52 DoF and 11-DoF hands. It has a $30,000/RMB 248,000 list price and mass-production announcements, but the evidence base is dominated by company claims and title-only demo videos. The strongest evidence is a company-described gait video on varied terrain with external pushes; commercial proof is weak despite a Zhaofeng Motor video title and confirmed orders, especially given low 2025 revenue and financial instability.
strongest_positive_evidence: Company-described gait-upgrade video showing stable walking over bricks, plastic and grass under external pushes (kepler-k2_evidence_014).
Confirmed orders over 47 million yuan reported by BigGo Finance (kepler-k2_evidence_016).
Official video title indicating an on-the-job log at Zhaofeng Motor (kepler-k2_evidence_021).
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No independent benchmark, autonomy audit, endurance log or safety certification.
No walking speed, battery capacity, or detailed task success rates.
Zhaofeng Motor deployment is only a video title, with no transcript or customer press release.
Most locomotion and manipulation demos have no teleoperation disclosure.
conflicting_claims: Productivity claim of 1.5 human workers is company-only and not independently validated.
Some source 4 language describes K2 as world's first commercially available hybrid-architecture humanoid, but no independent body confirms this.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit K2 as a fully autonomous system; autonomy is company-claimed and mostly not teleop-disclosed.
Do not treat Zhaofeng Motor as a confirmed customer deployment beyond the official video title.
Do not present framework agreements as delivered units.
Do not infer manipulation capabilities from title-only videos.
Do not use source 8 or source 12 for K2 evidence because K2 is not clearly specified.

currentness.currentness_notes: As of 2026-10-29, K2 Bumblebee is Kepler's commercial humanoid. The Kepler channel posted a Qilin debut video in September 2026, but no statement was found that it replaced K2.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Kepler K2 Bumblebee is a commercial industrial humanoid from Shanghai. It is 175 cm, 75 kg, 52 DoF, with 11-DoF hands, a hybrid roller-screw/rotary actuator design, 100 TOPS compute, and a claimed 30 kg dual-arm payload and 8-hour runtime on a one-hour charge. Kepler lists a $30,000 base price or RMB 248,000 and announced mass production and shipments in September 2025. The most concrete positive evidence is a company-described gait video showing the robot walking over bricks, plastic and grass and remaining stable under pushes. Commercial proof is limited: confirmed orders of over 47 million yuan are reported, and an official video title suggests a Zhaofeng Motor on-the-job log, but 2025 revenue was only 4.34 million yuan with heavy losses and the company was acquired at a lower valuation. Autonomy, endurance and manipulation claims are mostly company statements without independent verification; many demo videos are title-only with no teleoperation disclosure.
strongest_evidence: Company-described K2 gait demo on varied terrain with external pushes (kepler-k2_evidence_014).
Official video title indicating Zhaofeng Motor on-the-job log (kepler-k2_evidence_021).
weakest_evidence: No independent benchmarks, safety certification, or teleoperation disclosures.
No walking speed, battery capacity, or detailed autonomy data.
Zhaofeng Motor deployment is only a video title.
Financial data shows 2025 revenue of 4.34 million yuan and large losses.
known_do_not_credit: Do not credit full autonomy; autonomy claims are company-asserted.
Do not treat Zhaofeng Motor as a confirmed deployment beyond the video title.
Do not treat framework agreements as delivered units.
Do not infer capabilities from title-only videos.
Do not credit source 8 high-altitude welding or source 12 Qilin to K2.
